clue.text: Fellows hanging around us city with trendy clergy

indicators.note: hanging around means the word for fellows surrounds the next pieces

parts.note: fellows are chaps
LA (Los Angeles) is a city in the US
in means fashionable or trendy

explanation.surface: Men loitering near an American city alongside fashionable churchmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' is printed in lower case but stands for US, the United States, whose city is LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaplains are ministers attached to institutions, so they are members of the clergy; the plural matches.

clue.text: Woman — what can you do to a cold one?!

definitions.text: what can you do to a cold one?!

explanation.surface: A woman's name, then a cheeky question about warming someone chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical: split the name into two words and you get the remedy for a cold female.
explanation.definitionFit: Heather is a girl's name, and heat her is what one would do to warm a chilly woman.

clue.text: Face pain showing self-assurance

parts.note: pan is slang for the face
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Someone shows confidence while enduring a facial ache.
explanation.walkthrough: PAN is British slang for the face, as in 'deadpan'.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence and style, a showy form of self-assurance.

clue.text: See insect coming in harm a ground plant

indicators.note: coming in means the insect goes inside the rearranged letters
ground means crushed and reshaped, so the letters of harm and a are rearranged

parts.note: an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: Watch a bug causing damage to some crushed vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' turns HARM A into AMARH; 'coming in' puts ANT inside it, after AMAR. 'See' at the start is only a link inviting the solver to look.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaranth is a genus of flowering plants, some grown as grain or ornamentals.

clue.text: Man on vessel that floats around the Orient

parts.note: Sam is a man's name
a pan is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: A man aboard an eastern boat drifting about.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the man above the vessel. The definition is descriptive: a craft floating in eastern waters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampan is a small flat-bottomed boat used in China and Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Comment that's spun but snide, nothing in it?

indicators.note: in it means the letter for nothing is placed among the other letters
spun means twisted about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A political remark twisted by spin doctors, yet cutting and empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing in it' adds O to BUT SNIDE, and 'spun' rearranges all nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A soundbite is a short punchy remark or quotation, especially one made for broadcast.

clue.text: One article of clothing near another

parts.note: nigh means near
another article of clothing here is a tie

explanation.surface: A garment placed next to a second garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another article of clothing, the tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, a garment worn in bed.

clue.text: Easter egg that's melted set apart

indicators.note: melted means losing its shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chocolate Easter egg melted and was put aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'melted' rearranges the nine letters of EASTER EGG.
explanation.definitionFit: To segregate is to separate or isolate one group from others.

clue.text: Poison — it's found in an ice cream!

indicators.note: found in means the word it sits inside the word for an ice cream

parts.note: a cone is an ice cream served in a wafer cone
it is, giving the letters IT

explanation.surface: A warning that toxin has been discovered in an ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's found in' reads as 'it is found in': IT goes inside CONE, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, or monkshood, is a plant whose roots yield a deadly toxin.

clue.text: Happy about a sin — awful denial

definitions.note: used as a noun, a contradiction

indicators.note: about means the word for happy goes around the other letters

parts.note: gay in its older sense means happy

indicators.note: awful means badly done, so the letters of a sin are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheerful attitude to wrongdoing is dreadful denial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' turns A SIN into AINSA, which 'about' puts inside GAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gainsay, mostly a verb meaning contradict, is also an old noun for a contradiction or refusal.

clue.text: Gasp — the woman's a wild beast!

parts.note: to gasp is to pant
her is the possessive for the woman

explanation.surface: A startled cry that a woman is some kind of untamed creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A panther is a big cat, a leopard or jaguar, untamed and dangerous.

clue.text: Two short conversations before and after tea dance

parts.note: a conversation is a chat; short means it loses its last letter
cha is slang for tea
the second shortened chat

explanation.surface: Two quick chats either side of a cuppa, then a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts CHAT to CHA; 'before and after' places one each side of CHA, slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha-cha is a Latin American ballroom dance.

clue.text: The man must have a phone — it makes sense

parts.note: he refers to the man
to ring is to phone

explanation.surface: A man insists on owning a telephone because that's logical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it makes sense' is literal: one of the five senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing is one of the five senses, the faculty of perceiving sound.

clue.text: Empowering woman with jewellery

parts.note: Ena is a woman's name
bling is showy jewellery

explanation.surface: A woman feeling strong thanks to her jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Enabling means giving someone the power or means to act.

clue.text: Minister sticks his nose in, getting tense

parts.note: one who pries sticks his nose into others' business
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A government minister meddles and becomes edgy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' suggests a politician, but here it is a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest is a minister of religion.

clue.text: Charge outside city minimal amount? It's very steep

indicators.note: outside means the word for charge surrounds the next pieces

parts.note: a price is a charge
EC1 is a postcode of the City of London, with the 1 read as I
p, a penny, is a tiny sum

explanation.surface: A fee levied on the outskirts is tiny, yet the slope is sheer.
explanation.walkthrough: EC1 is a London postcode covering part of the City; its 1 becomes the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A precipice is a cliff face, a sheer drop.

clue.text: Boss a thrusting type? It's a sort of game

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised knob
a poker is something that thrusts or prods

explanation.surface: The boss is a pushy sort, all part of some game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' suggests an employer; it is a raised knob or stud.
explanation.definitionFit: Stud poker is a card game in which some cards are dealt face up.

clue.text: Theatre has been renovated at that place

indicators.note: renovated means rebuilt, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A theatre has been refurbished on that very site.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereat is an old word meaning there, in that location.

clue.text: Lay false claim to Yorkshire town, being cockney?

indicators.note: cockneys drop the letter H at the start of words

parts.note: Harrogate is a spa town in North Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Pretending to be a Londoner in a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrogate is a spa town in Yorkshire; 'being cockney' drops its H, as a Londoner from the East End would.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrogate is to seize or claim something without right.

clue.text: Mindless, like on sitting on square

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Mindless, like on sitting on square (7)': the wordplay needs AS + I + NINE, so 'on' should be 'one'; as held no word gives the I
annotationWithheld.clue: Mindless, like on sitting on square

clue.text: Sit again to get rest

explanation.surface: Posing once more for a portrait gives a chance to relax.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-pose is to model again; repose also means relaxation or rest.

clue.text: Praise from archbishop getting into bed

indicators.note: getting into means the archbishop goes inside the word for bed

parts.note: pit is slang for bed
William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I

explanation.surface: Acclaim from a senior cleric climbing into bed.
explanation.walkthrough: PIT is British slang for bed; Laud was a 17th-century Archbishop of Canterbury.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaudit is an expression of praise or approval.

clue.text: Not religious and construed as cruel

indicators.note: construed means interpreted or put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone irreligious is interpreted as heartless.
explanation.definitionFit: Secular means worldly, unconnected with faith.

clue.text: Demoralised actors now troubled about director

parts.note: the actors in a production are the cast

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Actors are now upset over the director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' mixes NOW with D to make DOWN; 'about' joins only.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast down means dejected, low in spirits.

clue.text: One achieving success with not the best of hits

parts.note: in archery or darts the inner ring scores less than the bull

explanation.surface: Someone succeeding despite middling shots.
explanation.walkthrough: An inner is the ring just outside the bullseye, a good but not top shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A winner is someone who triumphs or succeeds.

clue.text: Not knowing the answer!

parts.note: being unaware of the solution is the state of lacking knowledge

explanation.definitionFit: Ignorance is a lack of knowledge or information.

clue.text: Coming from ship on to one floating platform

indicators.note: Coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something emerging from a ship onto a raft.
explanation.definitionFit: A pontoon is a flat-bottomed boat or float used to support a bridge or landing stage.

clue.text: Fellow and boy brought back a form of eastern art

parts.note: a man is a fellow

indicators.note: brought back means the word for boy is read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A man and boy return with an example of Asian art.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandala is a circular symbolic design used in Hindu and Buddhist practice.

clue.text: Trick by offspring reportedly? Give up

parts.note: a con is a trick

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for offspring is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: seed means offspring, as in biblical descendants

explanation.surface: A swindle by one's children, so to speak, makes one surrender.
explanation.walkthrough: SEED, offspring, sounds like CEDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede is to yield or surrender.

clue.text: Dining room in parson's house? Only half feed in it

indicators.note: in it means the half word goes inside the parson's house

parts.note: a rectory is a parson's residence

indicators.note: only half means just the first half of the word feed is used

explanation.surface: A vicarage dining room where only half rations are served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only half' takes FE from FEED; 'in it' puts it inside RECTORY.
explanation.definitionFit: A refectory is a communal dining hall, as in a monastery or college.
